title: What's in That Bottle? Bonding in Unknown Solids
description: An Chemistry inquiry classifier in which students choose at least four qualitative and quantitative tests, validate a flowchart with 4-6 known solids, apply it to 4-6 blind unknowns, and justify bond type and identity reliability after the instructor release gate.
learningGoals: Design and obtain approval for a safe microscale panel of at least four qualitative and quantitative property tests.
Use 4-6 known solids to build and validate an evidence-based flowchart for ionic, metallic, polar covalent, and nonpolar covalent solids.
Classify 4-6 blind unknowns, quantify confidence and uncertainty, then match identities and SDS/MSDS only after instructor release.
safetyNotes: Wear splash goggles at all times and review the relevant SDS/MSDS for every assigned known and unknown.
Treat 0.1 M hydrochloric acid and 0.1 M sodium hydroxide as skin and eye hazards; use only teacher-approved microscale quantities.
Use hexanes or iodine only under teacher control in the hood when selected; keep organic-solvent work and waste in the approved hood workflow.
Use the conductivity tester only for metals and aqueous solutions; do not imply valid conductivity measurements for arbitrary dry nonmetal powders.
Place every solid and liquid in the teacher-labeled SDS-defined waste stream and reset or rinse the test station between fresh microsamples.
